newsitem.title: USA: IPO VIEW-U.S. IPO market still in holiday lull.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW-U.S. IPO market still in holiday lull.

text.p: Initial stock offerings were expected to stay in a deep freeze this week with only one company, Sun Hydraulics Inc., willing to venture into the new issues market, but activity should pick up later in the month, analysts say.

"This week there will be a lot of roadshows as they go out and bang the drums. It takes about two weeks for the dog-and-pony show to be dragged across the continent, and then IPOs could start popping like popcorn," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.
However, the choosy mood of the IPO marketplace is likely to continue this year, analysts say.

"I'm being very picky ... There's not much I consider to be interesting coming up and there's nothing next week I'm investing in. I'm certainly staying away from anything in technology that doesn't have a substantial earnings history," said Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities.
Fitzgibbon said another reason adding to the lethargy of the IPO market was its poor 1996 overall performance.
Despite record numbers of dollars raised, IPO aftermarket performance for the year was only 16 percent, he said, greatly lagging the major indexes.
For 1996 the Dow Industrials rose 26 percent and the Standard & Poor's Index rose 20.3 percent.
Sun Hydraulics, a maker of hydraulic cartridge valves, may be the first IPO of 1997 but is not expected to generate much enthusiasm from institutional investors, according to analysts.
The Sarasota, Fla., company plans to offer two milllion shares in a range of $9.50 to $11.50.
On Friday a company that owns and operates an outdoor theme restaurant on the waterfront in Philadelphia postponed its planned initial public stock offering.
Underwriter National Securities Corp. did not give a reason why Katmandu Entertainment Corp. cancelled its offering.
